flashcards.q: What is the Chinchilla compute-optimal token-to-parameter ratio?
flashcards.a: Roughly 20 tokens per parameter for a fixed compute budget C, where both optimal N and D scale as C^0.5.

flashcards.q: Why do modern production models train far past the Chinchilla-optimal ratio?
flashcards.a: Chinchilla minimizes training-loss-per-FLOP, not total cost of ownership; inference cost scales with parameters and is paid indefinitely, so a smaller model trained on more tokens is often cheaper overall.

flashcards.q: What token-to-parameter ratio did LLaMA-7B train at, and how does it compare to Chinchilla?
flashcards.a: About 143:1 (1T tokens / 7B params), roughly 7x the Chinchilla-optimal ratio for that model size.

flashcards.q: What did Muennighoff et al. (2023) find about repeating training data across epochs?
flashcards.a: Repeating up to ~4 epochs causes negligible degradation, gains continue with diminishing returns to ~16 epochs, and benefit is essentially gone by ~40 epochs.

flashcards.q: What MinHash/LSH configuration does FineWeb use for deduplication?
flashcards.a: 112 hash functions split into 14 bands of 8, over 5-gram shingles, at roughly a 75% Jaccard similarity threshold.

flashcards.q: Why does FineWeb deduplicate per crawl-snapshot instead of globally?
flashcards.a: Global dedup was found to systematically favor whichever snapshot was processed first/last, discarding valuable older content due to processing order rather than quality.

flashcards.q: State the compute-budgeting FLOP formula used for pretraining arithmetic.
What does 'curriculum' mean in modern LLM pretraining, as distinct from classic curriculum learning?
flashcards.a: Staged domain mixture -- broad web-dominated data first, then a smaller high-quality/curated/synthetic 'mid-training' stage -- not per-example easy-to-hard ordering.

flashcards.q: Why does curriculum (staged) pretraining need a different LR schedule than uniform-mixture training?
flashcards.a: Curriculum training needs a more moderate LR decay; reusing the uniform-training schedule can waste the value of the late high-quality stage.

flashcards.q: Name three static domain-mixture weighting approaches used before a full pretraining run.
flashcards.a: DoReMi, DoGE, and RegMix -- all fit domain weights using small proxy models before committing the full-scale run.

flashcards.q: What token-to-parameter ratios did Qwen3-0.6B and LFM2.5-350M reportedly reach?
flashcards.a: Qwen3-0.6B: 60,000:1. LFM2.5-350M (April 2026): 80,000:1, combined with large-scale RL.

flashcards.q: What risk does heavy synthetic data usage in pretraining mixtures carry?
flashcards.a: Model collapse -- a self-reinforcing quality degradation when synthetic data dominates the mixture; keeping it a minority (illustrative ~1:3 synthetic:natural) mitigates this.
